core.text: Preserve eight registrations and eight distinct recognitions by boundary 9, within six dispatcher actions. Six registrations and seven recognitions remain; the initial empty queue cannot deliver at tick 0.

Candidate: carry completed-registration IDs and their recognition/queue status through the readable ledgers to dispatch decisions, replacing the routine dashboard handoff. P1 still validates; P2 still requests and delivers through existing controls. This migrates informational coordination only: registration eligibility cannot move. Hypothesized benefit is avoiding stale N1 and already queued identities.

Concrete finite-model schedule: validate N3,N4,N5,N6,N7,N8 at ticks 0,1,2,3,4,5. Request N2,N3,N4 individually at 0,1,2; bulk at 4 queues N5,N6; request N7 individually at 5 and N8 at 6. Predicted deliveries: N2,N3,N4 at 1,2,3 and N5,N6,N7,N8 at 5,6,7,8. Six actions; N8 arrives during availability.

Compare five feasible interfaces using the same validation order and available controls: original dashboard with bulk requests at 0,1,2,4,5,6; transferred ledger decisions implementing the schedule; broken ledger handoff falling back to that original routine; co-presence with the successful schedule prescribed beforehand; and each parent alone. Measure registration count, distinct recognition, queue waste and actions. Ablate information sharing only; never remove mandatory registration eligibility.

residue.text: Closest rival is a fixed P2 control schedule requiring no live ledger handoff. It predicts eight recognitions in co-presence, matching transfer. Original and fallback bulk schedules predict three recognitions. Thus improved controls alone can explain the difference and defeat a carrier-interaction claim.

P1 alone predicts eight registrations and the initial one recognition; P2 alone can recognize only the two initially registered identities. Their physical eligibility dependence persists. No available carrier transfers that stipulated gate while leaving both parents unchanged.

Burden: six clerk validations and six dispatcher actions; ledger reads add no clerk labor by stipulation. No extra server, configuration access or communication channel exists. Delay origin and later sender adaptation remain unknown; no network trial or global-optimality proof supports the proposed coordination benefit.

tension.account_a: Live ledger-carried handoff contributes beyond the individual parent policies.
tension.account_b: A prescribed P2 control schedule accounts for the gain; live handoff adds no demonstrated effect.
tension.prediction_a: With parent controls matched, breaking informational handoff reduces distinct recognition below eight.
tension.prediction_b: Prescribed co-presence matches transferred eight recognitions; this counterexample defeats the strong interaction claim.
